questions.text: SELECT operation in SQL is equivalent to
questions.solution:
The SELECT list chooses columns, which is projection. Unlike relational algebra, SQL keeps duplicate rows unless DISTINCT is used.

Answer: the projection operation, except that SELECT in SQL retains duplicates

questions.text: A file is organized so that the ordering of data records is the same as or close to the ordering of data entries in some index. Then that index is called
questions.solution:
When the data file is stored in (nearly) the same order as the index entries, the index is called clustered.

Answer: Clustered

questions.text: In the LU decomposition of the matrix [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 2\\ 4&9 \end{bmatrix}[/latex], if the diagonal elements of U are both 1, then the lower diagonal entry [latex]l_{22}[/latex] of L is________.
questions.solution:
Crout form: [latex]\begin{bmatrix}2&2\\4&9\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}l_{11}&0\\l_{21}&l_{22}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&u_{12}\\0&1\end{bmatrix}[/latex]

- [latex]l_{11}=2,\; l_{11}u_{12}=2\Rightarrow u_{12}=1[/latex]
- [latex]l_{21}=4,\; l_{21}u_{12}+l_{22}=9\Rightarrow l_{22}=5[/latex]

Answer: 5

- f1 swaps copies only (call by value), so a = 4, b = 5 stay.
- f2 swaps through pointers: b = 6, c = 5.

c [latex]-[/latex] a [latex]-[/latex] b = 5 [latex]-[/latex] 4 [latex]-[/latex] 6 = [latex]-[/latex]5

Answer: -5

questions.text: What are the worst-case complexities of insertion and deletion of a key in a binary search tree?
questions.solution:
A BST can be skewed (a chain) with height n [latex]-[/latex] 1. Insertion and deletion may then walk the whole chain.

Answer: [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex] for both insertion and deletion
